prompt.text: True or false: Monomers can be composed of multiple atoms or molecular subunits.

questions.explanation: A monomer is a building-block unit; it is itself a molecule made of atoms (and may contain multiple functional groups or subunits).

prompt.text: The four classes of large biological molecules are:

questions.explanation: The four major classes of large biological molecules are carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids.

prompt.text: Which of the following is not considered a macromolecule?

questions.explanation: Lipids are important biomolecules but are not generally classified as true polymers/macromolecules the way the others are.

prompt.text: True or false: Lipids are considered polymers but are technically too small to be macromolecules.

questions.explanation: Lipids are not polymers of repeating monomers in the usual sense; the statement is false.

prompt.text: The four large classes of biological molecules always contain:

questions.explanation: Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids all contain C, H, and O (proteins/nucleic acids also have N, etc.).

prompt.text: What is the monomer unit for carbohydrates?
Which of the following is not a complex carbohydrate?

questions.explanation: Fructose is a monosaccharide (simple sugar). Starch, glycogen, cellulose, and chitin are complex carbohydrates (polysaccharides).

prompt.text: Which of the following is the monomer for proteins?

questions.explanation: Proteins are polymers of amino acids.

prompt.text: At what structure level is a protein generally considered functional?

questions.explanation: Tertiary structure (overall 3D fold of a polypeptide) is typically when a protein becomes functional; quaternary involves multiple polypeptides.

prompt.text: A nucleotide is composed of what?

options: Nitrogenous base, pentose sugar, phosphate group
Nitrogenous base, ribose sugar, phosphate group
Nitrogenous base, pentose sugar, triphosphate group
Nitrogenous base, ribose sugar, triphosphate group
questions.answer: Nitrogenous base, pentose sugar, phosphate group
questions.explanation: A nucleotide has a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group.
Purines have two rings: adenine (A) and guanine (G). Pyrimidines are C, T, and U.

prompt.text: True or false: The monomers of lipids are not considered molecules themselves.

questions.explanation: Lipid “monomers” such as fatty acyl chains are not standard repeating molecular monomers like sugars or amino acids.
In this course framing, lipid building blocks are treated as hydrocarbons (fatty acid chains).

prompt.text: Compared to saturated fats, unsaturated fats:

options: Have the maximum number of hydrogens bonded per carbon
Have at least one double bond
questions.answer: Have at least one double bond
questions.explanation: Unsaturated fats have one or more C=C double bonds, which kink the chain.

prompt.text: Which fat more greatly contributes to cardiovascular disease?

questions.explanation: Diets high in saturated fat are more strongly linked to cardiovascular disease risk than unsaturated fat.

options: Have a polar phosphate head group
Have 2 hydrocarbon chains per molecule as opposed to 3
Have 3 hydrocarbon chains per molecule as opposed to 2
questions.answer: Have 2 hydrocarbon chains per molecule as opposed to 3
questions.explanation: Triglycerides have three fatty acyl chains; phospholipids typically have two plus a phosphate head.
Steroids like cholesterol are recognized by a characteristic four fused hydrocarbon rings.

prompt.text: A function of cholesterol is to:

options: Provide cell structure within the cell
questions.explanation: Cholesterol is a precursor for steroid hormones (and also modulates membrane fluidity).
